A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MeshFT and MeshFT-Net study. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison, including matching retained content across renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulation results on analytic waves, physical consistency, OOD generalization, acoustic scattering, and structural ablations, including appendix results.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds heterogeneous-body and nonlinear-lattice experiments, further ablations, and scaling measurements.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Algorithm 1 retain the incidence-wired architecture, learnable metric and dissipation, general nonlinear formulation, quadratic implementation, and training objectives. State-dependent conservative coupling was already described and tested in v1. The added benchmarks do not introduce a distinct proposed algorithm or component.

E1.justification: Section 5.5 and Appendix D.6 add a nonperiodic heterogeneous deformable body with an internal hole and higher-amplitude OOD evaluation, plus FPU, damped phi-four, state-dependent edge-coupling, and sine-Gordon lattice tasks. The earlier shallow-water-style toy is retained as a renamed controlled ablation, rather than newly added.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the matched original experiments. MGN, MGN-HP, HNN, PI-MGN, FNO, and GraphCON already appeared in v1; the new benchmarks use applicable subsets of these methods. The new controlled model variants constitute ablations.

E3.justification: The added experiments introduce trajectory-based train/validation/OOD splits, 256-step rollouts, reference integration with eight internal substeps, and higher-amplitude testing. They also introduce energy relative MAE, monotonicity-violation and dominant-frequency diagnostics, and a separate reduced-budget scaling protocol. Settings for the retained experiments remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 5.6 and Appendix D.8 add an ablation separating spatial metric capacity from topology-fixed wiring on heterogeneous elasticity. A new irregular-mesh scaling sweep and damped-lattice rollout/error-map comparison provide additional analyses. The earlier principle-level and state-dependent-coupling ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Existing three- and five-seed reporting and the OOD mean-plus-standard-deviation table are retained. New experiments report means over three seeds, continuing an existing practice; no increased repeat count, new uncertainty estimator, confidence interval, or significance test is documented.

E6.justification: Matched original tables retain their numerical results, while Tables 6, 7, 12, and 13 add substantial new outcomes. For example, heterogeneous-body TSMSE is 4.91e-3 and damped-lattice TSMSE is 2.54e-4 for MeshFT-Net. On FPU, HNN has lower TSMSE than MeshFT-Net, 9.05e-3 versus 3.04e-2, while MeshFT-Net preserves momentum more closely. These are new-setting results, not improvements to earlier scores.

T1.justification: Theorem 3.3, Corollary 3.4, assumptions, proofs, and the electromagnetism derivation are retained across appendix renumbering. The new triangle example illustrates existing incidence, transpose, and energy-cancellation identities rather than adding or revising a theoretical result.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution summary, and conclusion retain the same claims about principle-derived local port-Hamiltonian reduction, topology–metric separation, physical fidelity, data efficiency, and extrapolation. The additional experiments expand support without redefining these core contributions.

C2.justification: The new ablation discussion distinguishes heterogeneous metric capacity, which affects constitutive accuracy and energy fidelity, from incidence symmetry, which supports momentum preservation. Appendix D.6 also interprets persistence across mesh resolutions and explicitly qualifies the approximate meshing procedure. These refine the existing interpretation.

D1.justification: v1 promises a later code release and mentions anonymous review supplements; v3 reports a public repository location in the abstract. Appendices D.6 and D.8 substantially expand reproducibility information with meshing procedures, material and nonlinear-system coefficients, trajectory counts, optimization settings, timing procedures, and the explicit ablation perturbation.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds He et al. (2026) on thermodynamically consistent latent dynamics, and the FDTD reference changes to the Taflove–Hagness textbook. The overall positioning remains stable. Updates such as the Hernandez preprint-to-publication entry concern the same existing work.

P1.justification: v3 adds a notation tutorial, inserts experimental subsections, renames the existing toy experiment, and reorganizes appendix labels around the additions. Affiliations and acknowledgements also change. Most existing scientific prose and the overall narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds a notation table, an oriented-triangle schematic, benchmark and ablation tables, a scaling table, nonlinear rollout/error maps, and momentum/energy curves. These substantially expand the visual presentation. Existing figures and tables are retained, with some relocation and renumbering.

improvement.justification: v1's broad applicability claims relied mainly on analytic waves, qualitative acoustic scattering, and a controlled nonlinear toy. The new heterogeneous and nonlinear OOD experiments and targeted topology–metric ablation substantially strengthen evidence beyond that setting. The FPU results also expose an accuracy–conservation tradeoff. Added setup details, notation guidance, and a reported public code location improve assessability and reproducibility, although the theoretical arguments and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged.
